transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I guess what brings me in is I’ve been feeling like I’m always moving from one thing to the next. Like I don’t really settle or just idle very well.

It wasn’t such a big deal before, or at least I could kind of work around it, but with the new work setup it’s become harder to hide, I think. I’m not trying to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been noticeable enough that I thought I should come in and ask about it.
Do you find it difficult to relax or feel restless most of the time?

Yeah… I mean, not all the time, exactly, but I do get that way. Like if I’m sitting through a training video at work, or even a slow appointment, I start feeling kind of boxed in. I’ll feel like I need to stand up, stretch, or at least keep my hands busy with something.

It’s not like I’m trying to be disruptive or anything. I can usually manage it, but relaxing and just sitting still doesn’t come very naturally, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot or feeling anxious, even when there isn’t an obvious reason for it?

I don’t think so… not in a big way, anyway. I mean, I worry about normal things, work stuff or getting things done, but I wouldn’t say I’m anxious for no reason most of the time.

Unless I’m missing something you mean by anxiety? I don’t want to answer it wrong, but it doesn’t feel like that’s the main thing for me.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy lately?

Not really, no. I mean, I have off days like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling sad all the time or stopped enjoying things.

I still like the things I usually like. If anything, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I don’t think it’s depression… if that’s what you’re asking.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks or tend to get distracted easily, especially when the task isn’t very interesting to you?

Yeah, I think that does happen. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I can focus sometimes, especially if it’s something active or interesting.

But in the longer coaching meetings, or if I’m reading through a new procedure at work, I’ll start out okay… and then after a few minutes I realize my eyes have been moving across the page, or I’ve been sitting there listening, but I didn’t really take in what was said. Then I have to kind of go back and catch up.

So yes, I guess I do get distracted that way, especially when it’s dry or not very engaging.
Looking back, did you notice these kinds of difficulties with restlessness or staying focused when you were a child, or did they start more recently as an adult?

I think it goes back pretty far, honestly. I wouldn’t want to blame everything on that, but… looking back, it wasn’t just something that started with this job or getting older.

In grade school, I remember teachers saying I was bright, but kind of careless. Like I’d make mistakes I probably shouldn’t have, or I’d be talking when I wasn’t supposed to. And I guess I had to be reminded to stay with my work.

At the time it didn’t feel like a “problem,” exactly, more like I just needed to try harder. But yes, I think some of it was there when I was a kid too.
